feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with a clear senior digital communications profile and a logical career progression at NACo. It reads professionally and shows breadth across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes and some tightening to reduce repetition across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a senior digital strategy/communications leadership brand.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at one organization with steady advancement from coordinator to director signals trust, growth, and depth.  
- Good use of specifics: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Clarity, Power BI, and the 10,000+ page migration add substance and technical credibility.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable results beyond activity: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include metrics on email growth, engagement, efficiency gains, campaign performance, video reach, or cost savings.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “content operations and enterprise web improvement” needs a comma after “operations”); “English (Native)” / “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically uneven—use parallel formatting such as “English (Native), French (A2 – Learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a few specifics that reflect the most recent Drupal/platform modernization work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” and tighten the opening around seniority and scope.
- Replace generic phrases like “expert in” with stronger, evidence-aligned language tied to digital strategy, CMS modernization, and cross-channel operations.
- Bring the intro closer to recent experience by referencing enterprise web platforms, governance, analytics, and mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel communications, CMS modernization, digital governance, and the workflows and analytics that support complex enterprise publishing environments. Brings deep experience in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies; keep the intro high-level and let skills sections carry the detail.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination also recur in work history, so avoid adding more examples here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, sharper phrasing and pluralize where appropriate: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial workflow design • Analytics & performance reporting • Workflow automation & systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Consider replacing generic terms like “data analytics” with “analytics & performance reporting” to align with the CV’s stronger evidence in GA4, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery.
- If space allows, swap “Web & CMS administration” for “Web platform modernization & CMS administration” to better reflect the Drupal migration and enterprise web work.
- Keep this section high-level; let Topline Skills and Technical + IT carry the tools and platform specifics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Digital strategy,” “multi-channel communications,” and “policy & advocacy communications” are already echoed in the header and Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting scope, senior advisory value, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or named initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; start with verbs like “Advised,” “Built,” “Led,” “Improved.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search relevance gains, stakeholder teams served.
- Separate strategic consulting from hands-on execution: one bullet for governance/operations, one for Drupal/campaign builds, one for AI search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” and “governance/usability best practices” repeat themes already covered in the 2022–2024 NACo role.
- Microsites, anniversary campaign, and AI search are also echoed in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same detail here unless tied to outcomes.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading team, strategy, governance, analytics and budget across web, email, social and video.”
- Combine the strongest web metrics into one bullet: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes sharper where possible: add budget size, team size, % efficiency gains, reporting cadence improvements, or production volume for the studio/video work.
- Tighten softer bullets: replace “Strengthened digital operations…” with specifics such as governance model launched, standards adopted, or planning system implemented.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo entries; emphasize building the in-house studio, not recurring video production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support than leadership. Tighten it around what changed under your ownership and add any concrete growth, cadence, or audience metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + outcome: “Led NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Make bullets more impact-led and parallel: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders” / “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace weak phrasing like “helped improve” and “strengthened” with clearer ownership: “Built editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy and program teams” and “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency and speed.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: open rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, stakeholder groups supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.
- Website/email/social oversight also appears in the 2022–2024 role; keep this one focused on operations and editorial systems.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms most tied to recent impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a long software list to a concise capability-led line: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” to connect with the 10,000+ page Drupal migration.

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led wording, e.g. “Analytics infrastructure & insight generation” rather than a pure software list.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider a stronger rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework design • Executive reporting and insight generation • SEO and digital performance optimization”
- If possible, align with recent impact from NACo by implying business use: reporting for leadership decision-making, optimization, and governance.

- Current wording duplicates the “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly.
- Avoid repeating dashboard/tool names elsewhere unless paired with outcomes in work experience.

items.title: University of Virginia

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this item to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeating a generic tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level of use: “Drupal (enterprise migration, modular builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Put the strongest/recent platform first and consider dropping the weakest/least strategic one if space is tight: Drupal should clearly lead.
- If accurate, add version/scope for credibility: “Drupal 10” or “Drupal (10,000+ page migration)” to connect with recent impact.
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“Drupal - WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages”). Differentiate by adding context/level here or remove one instance.
- GitHub Pages may read as lightweight beside enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, with cleaner phrasing and only tools you actively use in recent roles/projects.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API and webhook integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV is targeting hands-on developer roles; they add little value at your seniority.
- Use broader, outcome-oriented phrasing where possible: “API and webhook integrations” and “GitHub Actions/CI workflows” sound more applied than tool-only labels.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie 1–2 of these to recent work/projects (e.g., Drupal microsites, AI search, analytics implementation) rather than listing them in isolation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Consider removing this item entirely if Topline Skills already covers the same ground.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software dump and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it tighter and more systems-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to improve scanability: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams” for clarity and consistency.
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value/general collaboration tools if space is tight; prioritize tools tied to recent work and automation leadership.
- If you’ve built meaningful automations, replace one tool with a capability phrase: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, workflow design, cross-platform process automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis in both places.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; listing both may add less value than highlighting automation/integration depth.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational/email leadership context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email platform ownership, campaign execution, or member engagement use cases.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**.
- Reorder by likely depth/relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp** if Higher Logic was the primary NACo platform.
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **Higher Logic (member newsletters, segmented sends) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation) • Mailchimp (list/email campaigns)**.
- Keep platform names concise; consider shortening **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys** to **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights (Journeys)** for readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partially overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters; avoid repeating audience size or newsletter cadence here unless other technical items also include usage context.
- “Engagement” may overlap with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; keep this item tool-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with clearer scope and any available volume metrics.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if known: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or growth in production capacity.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and recurring video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a sharper full version: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, support a major website refresh, and improve multi-channel publishing workflows. Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and guided a junior digital staff member.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on team formation and hands-on production.
- Avoid repeating website leadership language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project support, and trim generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the multimedia line: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications materials.”
- Make the differentiator the final clause: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If available, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item lighter and more foundational.
- Avoid repeating broad web/email/social language here since those responsibilities are better established in 2015–2024 roles.
